# AI Artist Xania Monet Climbs the Charts — And Signs a Multimillion-Dollar Record Deal (Billboard)

By Hannah Karp. Published September 16, 2025.

## Key findings
- **Xania Monet** is the project of a **Mississippi-based design-studio owner** who used **Suno** to turn her lyrics into music. One label offered **$3 million** to sign her.
- The artist's real name is **Telisha Jones** (goes by Nikki), a poet; she used AI to craft her image and Suno to craft her music.
- Because she used Suno (sued for copyright infringement by the majors the prior year), labels backed by the majors abstained; one major put a top offer anyway. Bidding reached **$3 million**; **Hallwood Media** (led by former Interscope executive **Neil Jacobson**) ultimately signed her with a multimillion-dollar agreement.
- Monet appeared on the **Billboard charts** for the first time (week dated Sept. 20, 2025): **No. 25 Emerging Artists**, **No. 21 Hot Gospel Songs** with "Let Go, Let God."
- "How Was I Supposed to Know" hit **No. 1 R&B Digital Song Sales**, **No. 3 R&B/Hip-Hop Digital Song Sales**, **No. 22 Digital Song Sales.**
- Her catalog had earned **9.8 million on-demand official U.S. streams**, **5.4 million** of those in the most recent tracking week (Sept. 5–11), per **Luminate.**
- In July, Hallwood signed **imoliver**, the top-streaming "music designer" on Suno — the first signing of a Suno creator to a label. Its breakout single "Stone" had 3M+ Suno-platform streams before release (Aug 8).

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — Billboard is a top-tier / recognized domain authority in music; uses Luminate data.
- Establishes: Xania Monet = AI R&B artist created by Telisha Jones via Suno; $3M Hallwood Media deal; first Billboard chart entries (Sept 2025); 9.8M U.S. on-demand streams (Luminate). Note: R&B/gospel-leaning, not strictly hip-hop — relevant to sub-category (b) framing.
